title.purpose: The page title under the guide words; the only 27px text on a page.

headword.purpose: Entry titles, plate titles, glossary terms; followed by the mode as an italic part of speech.

body.purpose: Writing, ledes and replies on a 66-68ch measure; old-style figures, tabular lining figures for counts.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked capitals for guide words, section labels, plate numbers, thumb tabs and printed button text. Never a decorative kicker.

caption.purpose: 13px italic for plate captions, the page name in guide words, placeholders.

shadows.name: shadow-sheet
shadows.purpose: The one shadow: a loose sheet (dialog, tour card, Help, footnote popover) lying on the page.

focus.name: focus-ring
focus.purpose: Every focusable element, 13:1 or more on every ground.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: A page passing: decelerates and stops, no overshoot. Default for rises, pops and control colour changes.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Printed controls: hover to sunk stock, active prints reverse. Nothing moves.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.value: 180ms ease-out-expo, opacity 0 to 1 and translateY 8px to 0

motion.name: pop-in
motion.value: 180ms ease-out-expo, opacity 0 to 1 and translateY 6px to 0

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: The sealed stamp, printed onto the page.

motion.name: seal-blur
motion.purpose: Sealing an entry: rare and irreversible, the one heavier effect.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Honoured for both prefers-reduced-motion and the in-app data-reduce-motion override.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Guide words gain the centred page name; plate sides widen to 28px.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: 320px session column appears; mobile header and bottom nav retire.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: 104px shoulder thumb index appears on the right edge.

components.name: Headword Entry
components.description: A session in the list: bold title, italic mode as part of speech, then mood dot plus word and time.
components.html:
Sleep is the load-bearing one reflect.

steady·Oct 24

narrative.overview:
Aperture is set like a reference book its owner is writing. Each finished session is filed as an entry and set like a headword: a bold title followed by its mode in italic, the way a dictionary gives a part of speech. Every list of entries is headed by guide words (the first and last thing in view, with the page's own name set in italic between them) so a reader always knows which span of the journal is in front of them. The page is engraving ink on a cool bible-paper stock. Colour is kept to bordered, numbered plates, the way a reference book keeps its colour plates apart from the text.

Rank comes from apparatus, not size. One nineteenth-century "Modern" face is set at three sizes only. Hierarchy comes from bold, italic, tracked capitals and the weight of the rules between things: a 2px head rule, 1px ink rules and faint hairlines. Controls are printed marks: square, edged in ink, flat. The primary action is printed in reverse. Nothing floats, tilts or bounces. The only lifted object is a loose sheet (a dialog, the tour, Help) lying on the page.

The density is that of a well-set reference page: compact metadata at 13px, writing at 17px on a 66 to 68ch measure, and generous space where the writing happens. Day and Night are the same book printed on two stocks. Every ink pair passes WCAG AA in both.
keyCharacteristics: One serif family (Old Standard TT), three sizes: 13 / 17 / 27px.
Guide words head every list and every page.
Entries are headwords: bold title, italic mode as part of speech.
Ink on stock; colour only inside plates and mood marks, plus rubric for what is new until seen.
Square everywhere; the only round shapes are the mood dot, the unread mark and the "?" footnote mark.
One shadow, kept for loose sheets.

rules.name: The Colour-in-Plates Rule
rules.body: Pages are ink on stock. Plate inks appear in quantity only inside a bordered plate, and outside one only as a mood dot beside its word. If you can see colour that is not in a plate, a mood mark or rubric, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Three Moods Rule
rules.body: Mood is always a dot plus a word, in three discrete inks: emerald for lighter (valence above 0.25), madder for heavier (below -0.25), and violet for about level. Energy is carried by the dot's opacity (0.45 to 1.0), never by a fourth hue. Colour is never the only carrier.

rules.name: The Rubric Rule
rules.body: Rubric means "new until seen" or "this destroys or stops something". It is used for nothing else and never as a fill.

rules.name: The Three Sizes Rule
rules.body: 13, 17 and 27px, and nothing else. When something needs more rank, make it bold, italic, capitals or ruled, not bigger.

rules.name: The Part-of-Speech Rule
rules.body: A mode is always set in lowercase italic with a trailing full stop ("reflect.") wherever it names an entry or a choice.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one shadow, and it means "a loose sheet lying on this page". A control, plate or card that casts a shadow is wrong.

dos: Do head every page and every list of entries with guide words over a 2px ink rule.
Do set entries as headwords: bold title, then the mode as a lowercase italic part of speech with a full stop.
Do keep all text at 13, 17 or 27px, and gain rank from weight, italic, capitals and rules.
Do put any figure that needs colour in a numbered plate with an italic caption that explains how to read it.
Do show mood as a dot plus its word, in emerald, madder or violet only.
Do print the primary action in reverse (ink fill, stock text). Hover goes to sunk stock and active prints in reverse.
Do keep every control at least 44px tall on phones, and keep the 2px ink focus outline.
Do honour both reduced-motion paths (the OS setting and the in-app override). Motion is a short fade or an 8px rise that stops dead (180ms, expo-out), with no overshoot.
donts: Don't add a second type family or a fourth size.
Don't put colour on the page outside plates, mood marks and rubric. In particular, use no tinted cards or coloured section backgrounds.
Don't cast a shadow from anything that is not a loose sheet, and don't use hard offset shadows. Controls are printed, not stuck on.
Don't round corners. The only round shapes are the mood dot, the unread mark and the footnote mark.
Don't fill a destructive action with red. Say it in rubric.
Don't set a label-style line above a heading as a decorative kicker. Label type is for guide words, section labels and plate numbers.
Don't tilt, bounce or translate a control on press.
Don't recolour or crop the logo. It is the one full-colour picture, shown as-is and framed like a plate.
